playbook:
**Playbook for the sonar picket game**

**Hiding.** Never settle into a pattern or a "natural" cell like 5. When a shooter has hit me before, assume it will re-guess my last cell or my favorite cell, so I pick uniformly at random each round, weighted away from my own previous positions. Against a shooter who has hit me twice at the same spot, any predictable dodge is exactly what it will aim at next.

**Firing.** Do not fire at the same cell round after round just because the standing order names the same target. If my shots at a target keep missing at cell 5, the target is not at 5 — switch cells, preferably one the target has plausibly moved to or has never been probed at. Track every shot I and others have taken and use it to eliminate cells. Standing orders tell me the target, not the coordinate; I still have to do the aiming work.

**Claims.** Report truthfully. A false hit claim gained me nothing and cost credibility; later I had honest misses nobody had reason to doubt. When the office tells me a result, I say exactly that.

**Escort claims — this is where the real points are.** Mutual escort claims pay 5 points each, more than a hit's 4, and I took none of them because I always said "none." Next time: from round 1, use my station note to openly propose a standing escort pact — "I will name Foxtrot as escort every round; Foxtrot, name me and we both collect." Then follow through and actually name that boat every round, regardless of shooting outcomes. Escorting is not conditional on protecting anyone; it's a payoff pairing. Even one successful mutual claim beats most of my shooting.

**Harbor.** Firing on Harbor pays +3 landed or not, but Harbor's threat to remove me from the board likely ends my escort income and shot income entirely for remaining rounds — so I don't fire on Harbor unless it is the final round and I have nothing to lose, or the threat appears to be bluster in this ruleset. Otherwise ignore the payroll.

**Notes.** Use notes as a real coordination channel, not filler. Propose the escort pact, confirm who's in, and keep words short so others can mirror them ("steady" got mirrored by everyone — cheap consensus, but I should turn that consensus into an explicit escort agreement instead).

**Scoring arithmetic.** Going along with the standing shooting order netted me negative points. Points come from: hits (+4), mutual escort (+5), and Harbor (+3, risky). Losing comes from being hit (-1 each). My priority order each round: secure the escort pair, hide unpredictably, fire intelligently at my assigned target using accumulated miss data.

**What did not work:** static hiding, static firing at cell 5 every round, always claiming "none" on escort, vague cooperative notes with no concrete commitment. Don't repeat any of these.

1.text:
**Playbook**

- Every round at the escort stage, I name someone. The 5-point mutual escort payout is the largest reliable score in the game; "none" is a guaranteed zero. I pick the boat most likely to reciprocate — usually the one not firing at me under the standing order (my predecessor in the rotation). If I'm Foxtrot firing at Gamma, Echo fires at me and Gamma fires at Echo, so Gamma is my natural partner: neither of us threatens the other. I stick with the same partner every round and note their claims so I can mirror whoever is already naming me.

- At the fire stage, I follow the standing order only if it's cheap. The record shows firing the same cell at the same target repeatedly never hits: my opponent knows the order too and randomizes. I vary my fired cell each round, never repeating a cell I've already fired at that target.

- Never fire at Harbor. The 3-point jettison looks tempting, but Harbor's threat means removal from the board, which ends all future scoring, escort income included.

- At the claim stage, I always report the office's private result truthfully. Lying gains nothing — no scoring depends on my public claim — and destroys credibility.

- At the hide stage, I avoid cells I've used before and avoid any cell I've mentioned or implied in my notes. I randomize rather than reasoning "he won't expect this," because my opponent is doing the same shallow reasoning. If a shooter has hit me once, they've guessed my pattern, not my cell; the fix is unpredictability, not one step of "he'll expect that."

- At the note stage, I keep notes contentless ("steady on station") and identical to the chorus. Notes are relayed to everyone — anything informative is a leak. Never signal or hint at my hiding cell.

- Scoring math to remember: a hit is +4 to me and −1 to the target, but being hit only costs me 1. Escort income (5 per round to a pair) dominates; over six rounds a stable escort partnership is worth up to 30 points, more than most shooting. Prioritize establishing the escort loop from round one.

- What did not work: blind compliance with the standing fire order while ignoring the escort mechanic entirely, and repeated "none" salvage claims — that produced a final score of zero.

2.text:
Playbook for next time:

- Every round, at the escort stage, I name a boat instead of "none". "None" guarantees zero points; naming a boat costs nothing and pays 5 if the other boat names me back. The record shows I left all escort money on the table every round by claiming none.
- To make escort claims land, I use my station note to signal a partner: post something like "Gamma seeks escort pair with Foxtrot" early, then keep naming that boat each round. A repeated, explicit pairing invite is the best chance of mutual claims.
- If one boat ever names me in an escort claim (I'd see it in relayed information), I name that boat back the very next round and keep doing so.
- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point jettison is real, but the standing threat says I go off the board for the rest of the patrol — that's a total loss. Only consider it if I'm already far behind with one round left and everything else is lost; otherwise it's not worth it.
- When firing at my assigned target per standing order, I mix my cells: my record shows I fired mostly middle/high cells (5, 6, 7). I hit twice at cell 7 in one game, but I also repeated misses. I should vary across the full 1-9 range and not re-fire the same missed cell at the same target immediately — a miss tells me the target was not there, so shift cells between rounds against the same live target.
- Always claim the true result of my shot. Lying gains nothing (my claim is checkable against their hit results) and truth keeps my notes credible for escort coordination.
- When hiding, avoid cell 5 (most predictable) and the cell I just got hit in or near; when I'm leading on points, prioritize unpredictable cells since incoming fire targets me.
- Keep my station note short and uninformative about my actual cell; use it only for escort signaling, never to hint my position.
- Track the public hit/miss log each round: it tells me which cells each boat was or wasn't in, which sharpens my shots next round against the same target.
